title: Merge two sorted feeds
statement:
Two news feeds are singly linked lists of timestamps, each already sorted in non-decreasing order.

Merge them into one sorted linked list by relinking the existing nodes, and return its head. In tests, a list is written as an array of its values.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Should I reuse the existing nodes?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, relink them rather than allocating new ones.
clarifyingQuestions.why: Sets the O(1) extra space goal.

hiddenConstraints: Each list has up to 50 nodes in tests, but think about long lists.

edgeCases.why: After one list runs out, attach the rest of the other.
Either order is valid; taking from the first list keeps it stable.

approaches.name: Collect and sort
approaches.idea: Put all values in an array, sort, rebuild.
approaches.tradeoffs: Ignores that the inputs are already sorted.

approaches.name: Two-pointer merge with a dummy head
approaches.idea: Compare the heads, attach the smaller to a tail pointer, advance. A dummy node avoids special-casing the first node.

optimal.name: Dummy head merge
optimal.explanation: Create a dummy node and a tail pointer. While both lists have nodes, attach the smaller head (the first list on ties) to tail and advance that list and tail. Then attach whichever list remains. Return dummy.next.

hintLadder: Which node must come first in the merged list?
After you take a node, what is the next comparison?
How can you avoid special-casing the very first node?
Use a dummy head and a tail pointer, always attaching the smaller head.

expectedMentions.what: Describes the two-pointer merge and O(n + m) time
Explains why a dummy head simplifies the code
Remembers to attach the remaining list at the end

walkthrough.say: Either list could be empty? And I should relink the existing nodes rather than create new ones?
Both lists are sorted, so the smallest remaining value is always at one of the two heads. I compare the heads, take the smaller, and repeat. That’s O(n plus m) time, O(1) extra space.
I’ll use a dummy node at the front so I don’t have to special-case choosing the first node.
Attach the smaller head to the tail. On a tie I take from a, which keeps the order stable.
When one list runs out, the rest of the other is already sorted, so I attach it directly.
walkthrough.code:
tail.next = a or b
    return dummy.next

walkthrough.say: For 1, 4, 9 and 2, 4, 10: take 1, then 2, then the 4 from a, then the 4 from b, then 9. Now a is empty, so attach 10. Result 1, 2, 4, 4, 9, 10.
If a is empty, the loop doesn’t run and tail.next is b, so I return b. Both empty returns null.
O(n plus m) time and O(1) extra space.
